vignette:
Fernando was a 54-year-old business owner with a deep commitment to humanitarian work. His life had been shaped by his experiences as a relief worker in a war zone, where he dedicated years to providing aid in some of the most dangerous regions. The trauma he encountered, however, had seeped into his daily existence, overshadowing the man he used to be. 

The event that haunted Fernando was not a single moment but a series of harrowing experiences that culminated one fateful day. He vividly recalled the chaos of a bustling marketplace, one he had visited often to deliver supplies. It was supposed to be a routine day, but everything changed when gunfire erupted. The sound of bullets filled the air, accompanied by the frantic cries of people scrambling for safety. In that instant, Fernando felt an overwhelming sense of helplessness as he witnessed a child being struck. The scene replayed in his mind relentlessly, an uninvited guest that refused to leave. 

In the years following that day, Fernando found himself grappling with a myriad of emotions. Positive moments, once a source of joy, now confused him. He would feel laughter bubbling up at gatherings with friends or during family dinners, yet it would be quickly snuffed out by a dark shadow of guilt. "How can I be happy when others are suffering?" he would ask himself, his heart heavy with the weight of his memories. The cognitive dissonance was jarring; the very notion of joy felt like a betrayal to those he could not save.

Gunshots, once a distant echo of his past work, transformed into a trigger that sent his heart racing. Even the faintest sound resembling a bang would transport him back to that marketplace. If he was in a crowded place, like the restaurant he owned, a sudden noise could leave him frozen, scanning his surroundings with heightened alertness. The anxiety that gripped him was palpable, as he feared another eruption of violence. The physical proximity of others became overwhelming; he often found himself retreating to the back of his restaurant, seeking refuge from the throngs of customers. What frightened him most was the thought of being unable to protect his family or employees, mirroring the helplessness he felt years ago.

Over time, Fernando developed maladaptive strategies to cope with the turmoil inside him. He often reflected on the events that had unfolded, ruminating on why he had been spared while others had suffered. This obsessive questioning consumed hours of his day, leading him to isolate himself from loved ones. Friends noticed his absence; he became a ghost in his own life, more present in his memories than in the world around him. The weight of his thoughts turned into a burden he could no longer carry alone.

In an attempt to feel a semblance of control, Fernando began to carry a weapon. He justified it as a means of protection, a way to ensure that he would never again feel that helplessness. However, this only deepened his anxiety and further isolated him from his family, who were frightened by his behavior. Arguments would erupt with his wife, Sofia, often stemming from his need to create drama to distract himself from the pain. "You don't understand! I have to be prepared!" he would shout, the conflict serving as a temporary escape from the turmoil within. Yet each confrontation widened the chasm between them, and the strain on their marriage was palpable.

As months turned into years, Fernando found himself standing at a crossroads. The memories of his past and the strategies he employed to cope were no longer enough. He felt trapped in a cycle of fear and self-doubt, longing for the man he used to be. The turning point came when he overheard Sofia speaking with a friend about the toll his behavior was taking on their family. "He's not the same man I married," she said with a sadness that pierced his heart. In that moment, Fernando realized that he could not continue living this way. 

Seeking help felt daunting, but he could no longer ignore the pain that had woven itself into the fabric of his life. Fernando hoped that therapy could help him disentangle the memories that had ensnared him, allowing him to reclaim the joy he once felt. Yet he was equally terrified of confronting the very experiences he had buried for so long. The prospect of unraveling the trauma filled him with dread, but the thought of losing his family pushed him to take that first step toward healing.
